Key figures included Vans' first Global Music Ambassador, Anderson .Paak, whose involvement was announced in July 2022. Recent related events (events are separated by numbered tags): <1> A report from Buy Now, Pay Later (BNPL) service Afterpay revealed a significant rise in back-to-school shopping on its platform during May, June, and July of 2023. The data indicated a clear trend of consumers, primarily millennials, utilizing BNPL for school-related expenses. Specific year-over-year increases included a 65% rise in backpack sales and growth of over 100% for items such as "school shorts" and low-top sneakers. [1] An Afterpay spokesperson confirmed that spending grew across multiple categories including accessories, apparel, electronics, footwear, and home furnishings. [1] <2> A U.S. Chamber of Commerce report, published on July 30, 2024, analyzed key back-to-school shopping trends for the year, highlighting that the season is the second-biggest sales driver after the holidays. [2] The report incorporated projections from the National Retail Federation (NRF), which were also released on the same day. [1, 2] These projections estimated total spending to reach $38.8 billion for K-12 students and $86.6 billion for college students. [1, 2] Both reports noted a trend of consumers being price-conscious, actively looking for deals, and starting their shopping earlier in the season, with over half of shoppers having begun by early July. [1, 2] <3> Multiple states held back-to-school sales tax holidays in 2024, allowing consumers to purchase certain items tax-free. Alabama's 19th annual holiday occurred from Friday, July 19, to Sunday, July 21, 2024. During this period, the state's 4% sales tax was waived on items including clothing up to $100, school supplies up to $50, books up to $30, and computers or tablets up to $750. Many, but not all, local municipalities also waived their local taxes. The Missouri Department of Revenue announced its annual back-to-school sales tax holiday was scheduled for Friday, August 2, through Sunday, August 4, 2024. For this event, both state and local sales taxes were waived on qualifying items such as clothing valued at $100 or less, school supplies up to $50 per purchase, and personal computers up to $1,500. In 2024, 19 states were scheduled to hold some form of sales tax holiday. <4> Kohl's announced its 2024 back-to-school offerings, emphasizing value and style with hundreds of classroom essentials priced under $20. The campaign, which was revealed on July 12, 2024, also introduced new brands such as Limited Too and Aéropostale, alongside an expanded collection from Madden Girl. For college-bound students, Kohl's featured dorm essentials, including decor and storage, with prices starting at $9.99, and furniture and lighting under $50. The retailer highlighted deals on its private-label brands, with kids' Jumping Beans tees starting at $6.99 and SO denim from $19.99. The announcement also noted the availability of popular brands like Nike, adidas, and Under Armour, as well as savings opportunities through Kohl's Cash and Kohl's Rewards. This is supported by the fact that over 75% of parents expected to have begun their back-to-school shopping by July. <6> The Boys & Girls Clubs of America's local chapters conduct annual "Stuff the Bus" events, often as part of a broader "Back2School" initiative, to collect school supplies for children in need. [11] Similarly, the Boys & Girls Clubs of Broward County in Florida holds an annual event; in 2023, it took place on August 5 in partnership with Gunther Volkswagen and Audacy, a collaboration planned again for August 5, 2024. [9, 14] In nearby Palm Beach County, the local club partners with Office Depot and GL Homes for an annual Back to School Drive, which will run from June 2 to August 1 in 2025. [2, 4] These campaigns aim to ensure students have the necessary tools for academic success. Citing a National Retail Federation (NRF) survey, the report noted that as of early June, 22% of parents and students had already started their shopping for the 2024-2025 school season. The report emphasized the impact of inflation on spending, with a survey from Ibotta indicating that 98% of consumers would be looking for deals on at least one category of items. Furthermore, the rising cost of supplies, which increased by 23.7% over the past two years according to a 2023 Deloitte survey, has led 68% of shoppers to plan their purchases around major sales events like Prime Day and Labor Day. The growing importance of online shopping was also a key theme, as it offers convenience and price comparison opportunities for budget-conscious families. A separate 2024 survey by Prodigy Education found that parents anticipated spending an average of $333 on back-to-school items, a 6% increase from the prior year, with 65% of parents identifying rising costs due to inflation as their primary shopping challenge. <8> The United Way of Miami-Dade is holding its yearly Back-to-School Drive to provide necessary school supplies to students in need for the 2024-2025 academic year. The organization is accepting both physical supplies and monetary donations to assist low-income children and families served by various United Way programs. Donations of items can be dropped off at the United Way Miami building through Monday, July 29, 2024, and items purchased from their Amazon Wish List should be delivered by Wednesday, July 24, 2024. A key event of the drive is the backpack packing day, which will take place on Saturday, August 3, 2024, where volunteers will help organize and fill backpacks for students. This initiative aims to equip over 1,000 children with the tools they need for academic success. <9> On June 20, 2024, Coresight Research published its 'US Back to School 2024: Retail Outlook' report. This report is part of a series on the 2024 back-to-school season and provides spending projections, an analysis of the consumer landscape, and identifies key trends expected to influence the shopping period. The analysis includes proprietary survey data on consumer expectations regarding personal finances and the economy. <10> An analysis of 2024 back-to-school marketing trends advised marketers to launch their campaigns between mid-May and early June to effectively target early shoppers. [1] This recommendation is based on the finding that the back-to-school sales period commences in early July, with a significant majority (55%) of consumers starting their shopping at that time. [1]

metadata.original_text: This time series records back to school data in the web search domain, with a collection frequency of weekly, focusing on monitoring and analyzing relevant indicators. Prediction target period: from 2025-12-21 to 2026-03-08. Recent related events (events are separated by numbered tags): <1> A retrospective analysis published by EssayShark detailed that U.S. back-to-school spending for 2025 dropped slightly to an estimated $30.9 billion. Reflecting consumer behavior during the September back-to-school season, the report noted that families prioritized essential items amid a 7.3% year-over-year surge in the average cost of school supplies. <2> On November 25, 2025, Burlington Stores released its financial results for the third quarter ended November 1, 2025. The company noted that store traffic experienced a significant drop immediately following the back-to-school shopping period, driven by unseasonably warm temperatures across its major markets. <3> Ross Stores reported its third-quarter fiscal 2025 financial results, highlighting an 'excellent' back-to-school shopping season. The company noted that strong sales trends during this period contributed to broad-based growth. <4> Target Corporation reported its Q3 2025 earnings, highlighting strong sales performance driven by key seasonal moments such as back-to-school and back-to-college shopping. Target's fiscal year typically ends in late January, meaning its third quarter generally spans from August through October. <5> The National Retail Federation (NRF) released its 2025 holiday sales forecast, predicting that retail spending in November and December will grow between 3.7% and 4.2% over 2024. Alongside this projection, the NRF retrospectively noted that the 2025 back-to-school shopping season experienced near-record levels of consumer spending. <6> Euromonitor International published its Q3 2025 Engagement Index report, revealing that US apparel retailer Old Navy achieved one of the largest gains in digital customer engagement globally, driven in part by successful back-to-school campaigns. <7> The Commerce Department announced that U.S. retail sales exceeded expectations in August 2025, rising by 0.6%, the same rate as the upwardly revised figure for July. This growth, fueled by back-to-school shopping, demonstrated consumer resilience despite concerns over tariffs and inflation. The increase was notably supported by a 2.0% rise in online sales and a 1.0% growth in clothing store sales. Core retail sales, which exclude volatile sectors like automobiles and gasoline, saw a significant increase of 0.7%. Economists noted that while the figures suggest underlying strength, a weakening labor market and potential price hikes from tariffs could slow momentum in the future. <8> A wave of cyberattacks impacted U.S. school districts at the start of the 2025-2026 academic year, timed by attackers for maximum disruption. One of the most significant incidents targeted South Lyon Community Schools in Michigan, which detected a "network security incident" on Sunday, September 14, 2025. The breach crippled essential systems, including phones and network communications, forcing the district to close for three consecutive days, affecting 8,400 students across 12 schools. Classes resumed on Thursday, September 18, 2025, after significant progress was made in restoring the systems. This attack was part of a broader trend; another incident reported around the same time involved the Uvalde Consolidated Independent School District in Texas, which canceled classes for a full week due to a ransomware attack. According to a July 2025 report from the cybersecurity website Comparitech, ransomware attacks against educational institutions globally rose by 23% year-over-year in the first half of 2025, with 130 incidents recorded.
